title: Customer beta plan for Private upgrade/rollback (select 1–2 customers + success criteria + schedule)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Overview
We need a tightly scoped beta with 1–2 Private customers to validate the end-to-end upgrade + rollback workflow (prechecks → backup/verify → staged apply + gates → observability/diagnostics → rollback hooks) across both VPC and (optionally) air-gapped on-prem.

This ticket is the operating plan: which customers, what we will run, success criteria, schedule/maintenance windows, and how beta findings flow back into the backlog + release gates.

Primary stakeholders
- Beta pilots lead: Markus Klein
- Program mgmt: Talia Benson (owner)
- Release orchestration: Connor O’Brien
- Control plane/upgrade: Ethan Park
- Installer/tooling: Devon Price
- SRE/runbook: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Support enablement: Dev Patel / Owen Phillips
- Security: Marcus Lin / Dr. Aisha Rahman (bundle signing / audit requirements)

References / working links
- Confluence: Private upgrade framework overview (upgrade phases, ordering, invariants)
- Confluence: Upgrade prechecks spec
- Confluence: Backup and restore strategy
- Confluence: Rollback policy and downgrade compatibility
- Confluence: Offline upgrade bundle format (air-gapped)
- Confluence: SRE runbook for private upgrades
- Confluence: Upgrade observability and diagnostics
- Linear: PM-482 (PRD)

Beta goals (what we must learn)
1) Operator UX + safety: Can the customer run the workflow with minimal Redwood involvement using the runbook + installer UX? Where are the confusing/unsafe edges?
2) Real-world prechecks: Do prechecks correctly detect readiness issues (storage class, snapshot perms, disk pressure, k8s versions, drift) with actionable remediation?
3) Backup duration + reliability: Do backups complete within a reasonable maintenance window for their environment? Is verification meaningful (not a no-op)?
4) Rollback correctness: If we inject failures mid-upgrade, do we reliably rollback to a known good version without data loss or split-brain?
5) Diagnostics/supportability: Are logs + metrics + diagnostics bundle sufficient for Support to triage without jumping on a screen share?

Candidate customers (proposed)
We will run with one VPC customer first; add a second air-gapped customer only if offline bundle + signing path is ready.

Customer A (VPC): “Northbridge Health” (existing Private VPC deployment, planning minor→minor upgrade)
- Rationale: Has real traffic but can schedule a maintenance window; previously reported migration-step fragility; good fit to validate backup + schema gating.
- Owner: Markus Klein (PS) + Dev Patel (Support)
- Notes: Ensure snapshot/IAM permissions are validated early; they have strict least-privilege requirements.

Customer B (On-prem air-gapped, optional / stretch): “Helios Aero Systems” (air-gapped lab environment)
- Rationale: Validates offline bundle import + signature verification + no external registry access.
- Owner: Markus Klein + Bruno Silva
- Condition to include: Offline bundle import flow + verification behavior must be stable, and signing key custody + rotation story must pass security review.

Customer selection criteria (must-have)
- Has a non-production environment that matches production topology closely enough for a rehearsal.
- Can grant limited-time access for PS (screen share) and provide infra details needed for prechecks (k8s version, storage class, snapshot permissions, object store endpoints).
- Will commit to a maintenance window (2–4 hours) and accept a “beta limitations” disclaimer (no guarantee of zero downtime; rollback window constraints apply).
- Accepts data protection requirements: agreed RPO/RTO expectations and confirms backup storage location/retention.

Beta scope (what we will do)
Run two rehearsals per customer environment:
A) Dry run + prechecks-only
- Run installer prechecks in “read-only” mode.
- Export JSON report for Support ingestion.
- Validate remediation messaging is sufficient.

B) Full upgrade rehearsal (with defined failure injection)
- Take backup + verify.
- Execute staged upgrade (control plane → runtime → gateways → observability agents) with readiness gates.
- Validate smoke test gates + rollback boundaries.
- Inject one failure (choose based on environment):
  - Image pull failure / registry auth
  - Disk-full simulation on a worker
  - Schema migration marked forward-only when attempting rollback
  - Control plane API unavailable mid-step
- Confirm the operator can either abort safely or rollback safely.

C) Rollback rehearsal (explicit)
- Trigger rollback (manual command) from a known safe point.
- Confirm downgrade constraints are correctly enforced when migrations are forward-only.
- Confirm “previous known good version” is surfaced clearly.

Success criteria (beta exit)
Operational
- Upgrade completes successfully in customer staging in <= 90 minutes wall-clock (excluding customer-specific snapshot slowness) OR we produce a documented reason + mitigation.
- Rollback (when allowed by migration policy) restores service health within 30 minutes and returns component versions to previous known-good set.
- No critical data loss; backup verification passes and restore drill is credible (at least control plane DB restore validated).

Product/UX
- Prechecks catch at least one real customer issue before the upgrade step begins, and the remediation text is actionable.
- Installer outputs:
  - A single correlation id for the run
  - Step graph / plan is understandable
  - Clear “what to do next” on failure (retry vs abort vs rollback)

Supportability
- Diagnostics bundle includes: precheck report, step timings, relevant k8s events, and recent pod logs for involved components.
- Support can triage the injected failure using diagnostics + runbook without engineering intervention (timeboxed goal: <= 30 minutes to identify root cause category).

Security/compliance
- For on-prem/offline: bundle signature verification is enforced; failure mode is safe (no partial apply) and error message clearly describes what failed (signature, cert chain, manifest mismatch).
- Upgrade/rollback actions generate audit log events (who/when/from→to versions).

Beta schedule (proposed)
Week 1: Customer A readiness + dry run
- D1–D2: Selection confirmation + NDAs/approvals + identify environments
- D3: Precheck-only run + remediate
- D4: Freeze upgrade target version + gather baseline metrics

Week 2: Customer A full rehearsal
- Maintenance window: 2–4 hours (customer local time)
- Run full upgrade rehearsal + one injected failure + rollback rehearsal
- Post-mortem doc + backlog items filed within 48 hours

Week 3 (optional): Customer B (on-prem/offline)
- Only if offline bundle path + signing review are cleared
- Precheck-only run first; full rehearsal in separate window

Comms plan
- Customer-facing
  - Provide a 1-page beta brief: goals, expected downtime, rollback limitations (esp. forward-only migrations), and support escalation path.
  - Share maintenance window checklist (what to monitor, who is on-call, expected step durations).
- Internal
  - #eng-releases go/no-go 24 hours prior
  - #support heads-up with diagnostics bundle location + triage rubric
  - Incident bot tagging enabled for “upgrade-related” for rehearsals

Feedback loop into backlog
- All beta findings must be captured as:
  - New Linear issues with repro steps + logs/diagnostics references
  - Severity tag: Beta-Blocker vs Beta-Polish
  - Owner + target release
- Beta-Blockers gate GA checklist (ENG-2323).
- Beta-Polish can ship post-GA only if they do not affect safety, auditability, or supportability.

Risks / open questions
- Snapshot permissions on VPC: ensure we have a minimal IAM policy template ready and validated.
- Backup duration vs maintenance window: if DB snapshot time dominates, document recommendations (incremental snapshots where available; schedule guidance).
- Rollback constraints: make sure customers understand that forward-only migrations cannot be rolled back; we need a crisp UX that prevents “unsafe rollback” attempts.

Action items (next 7 days)
1) Markus Klein: confirm Customer A + tentative window; identify customer operator contacts.
2) Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes: validate runbook is runnable end-to-end without tribal knowledge; flag missing steps.
3) Devon Price: ensure installer supports --json output for prechecks + emits correlation id in all steps.
4) Dev Patel: draft Support triage checklist for upgrade failures using diagnostics bundle.
5) Marcus Lin: confirm signing key custody expectations for any offline bundle pilot.

Definition of Done
- Customer(s) selected and confirmed in writing with agreed maintenance window(s).
- Success criteria agreed internally (PM + SRE + Release Eng) and shared with customer(s).
- Rehearsal(s) executed (or scheduled with explicit go/no-go preconditions) and post-rehearsal notes captured.
- Backlog updated: at least one concrete beta outcome filed (bug/UX gap/docs gap), prioritized, and linked to GA readiness checklist.
